tldr: Lois Neistat (Concerned Oregonians) argues Oregon's 40 years of progressive policy have driven economic decline, advocating deregulation, tax cuts (income, capital gains, CAT, estate tax), 10-year PERS reform via matched funding, and education vouchers. The submission also includes supporting analysis from higher education, agriculture, and Southern Oregon perspectives on underfunding, regulatory burdens ($696/acre for pear growers), and economic development through placemaking.

bullets.text: Eliminate mandatory paid vacation, paid leave, and statewide rent control regulations
Eliminate the corporate activity tax, which has driven up costs for companies and individuals
Reform PERS over 10 years by earmarking capital gains tax, estate tax, and excess income tax revenue; provide agencies 2-to-1 or 3-to-1 matching funds for PERS liability reduction
Implement education voucher system: students receive 85% of per-student state funding for any public or private school; public schools funded by remaining 15% and student enrollment
Reduce capital gains tax from 9.9% to 3.9%; eliminate estate tax or increase exemption to $15 million per person
Cap government spending growth to inflation + 1% per year; reduce income tax rate from 9.9% to 9%
Oregon public universities face negative ending cash balances by 2031 without changes; OSU estimates $1 state investment yields $13 in economic activity
November 2025 OSU study finds small pear growers pay $696 per acre in regulatory compliance costs, representing 6.6% of total revenue
Oregon ranks 47th in business friendliness, 43rd in cost of doing business, and 45th in cost of living per CNBC rankings
